hero.title: Between lake and mountains
hero.text: Since 1957, authentic cuisine overlooking Lake Como and the Alps. Polenta, tradition, and a breathtaking panorama.

intro.title: An authentic place, built with passion
intro.text1: Polentoteca Chalet Gabriele is located in Piano Rancio, at the foot of Mount San Primo. Built in 1957 by Nuccia and Gabriele, the restaurant has always aimed for simplicity, quality, and courtesy.
intro.text2: Two dining rooms with large windows overlooking Lake Como and the Alps. A place where time slows down.

signature.title: Polenta, queen of the table
signature.text1: Polenta is the undisputed star of our menu. Prepared according to a family recipe, served with rich sauces and authentic flavors of the Lombard mountain tradition.
signature.text2: Alongside polenta, a rich menu of local specialties to satisfy every palate, from meats to alpine cheeses.

panorama.title: The lake, the Alps, your table
panorama.text: After lunch, take a walk in the woods or head down to Bellagio to admire the lake.

opening.title: A place built with hands and heart
opening.lead: It's not just a restaurant. It's a place that has existed for almost seventy years, built stone by stone by a mountain family, remaining true to itself when everything around was changing.

story.caption: Mariuccia and Gabriele, 1960s
story.title: Gabriele and Nuccia, a family story
story.p1: It was 1957 when Gabriele Galli, son of farmers from Bellagio, decided to open a small bar in Piano Rancio. Alongside him, Mariuccia Sala — known to all as Nuccia — Milanese by birth but with a mountain soul.
story.p2: What started as a village bar slowly transformed, season after season, into a restaurant. Not out of ambition, but out of necessity: people came up here, sat down, and asked for food. And Nuccia cooked.
story.p3: Their goal was simple and has never changed: simplicity, quality, and courtesy. Three words that still guide every working day today.

toc.title: Il Tóc, the soul of Bellagio
toc.p1: Tóc is the traditional dish of Bellagio par excellence, with over 150 years of history. The name comes from the local dialect "Tucà" — to touch — because it is eaten with hands, directly from the cauldron, together.
toc.p2: Cornmeal polenta, genuine butter, and alpine cheese slowly mixed to obtain a creamy and homogeneous mixture. A preparation that requires time, patience, and the expert hand of a true tocchista. If a step is missed, the Tóc releases the butter and is no longer edible.
toc.p3: For centuries it was prepared only for weddings and baptisms. Today we bring it to the table for groups upon reservation, with the ritual intact: the copper cauldron in the center, wooden spoons, and laughter all around.
toc.acc4: Ragèl — the digestive in the cauldron
toc.note: Available upon reservation for groups of at least 8 people

identity.title: Three things that will never change
identity.c1Text: We are a family cooking for other families. Since 1957, the same hand, the same care, the same way of being in the dining room: as if every table were our home.
identity.c2Text: Tóc is not prepared by reading a piece of paper. You learn by watching, refine it over time, carry it forward with respect for those who invented it. Only a true tocchista knows when it's ready.
identity.c3Text: Here you never eat alone in the true sense of the word. The restaurant is always full, the tables close, laughter mixing. A Sunday at the Polentoteca feels like a party even when it's not.

closing.title: Almost seventy years and the same cauldron
closing.p1: Gabriele and Nuccia are no longer here, but the spirit with which they opened this place has remained intact. The kitchen still works as it did then: real raw materials, local recipes, no shortcuts.
closing.p2: Those who come up here know it. You don't come to the Polentoteca by chance. You come because you heard it's worth the climb. And every time you leave with the feeling of having eaten something real.

arrive.title: Between lake and mountain
arrive.p1: The restaurant is located in Piano Rancio, a small town at the foot of Mount San Primo. The windows of the two dining rooms overlook Lake Como and the Alps surrounding the two branches of the lake.
arrive.p2: Easily accessible by any means, either by car along the provincial road or on foot along the forest paths. A large free car park is available for guests.
